summary:
We built the Earth Information Jukebox, a 3D globe you can explore by sound as well as by sight. We were frustrated that NASA’s Earth data is almost always shown as maps and charts, which leaves out anyone who can’t easily read them, and which can feel a bit distant for everyone else.

The globe has three modes. In Weather Moods, you click a country, see its live temperature and wind, and hear a song matching its current weather, drawn over NASA’s precipitation data. Climate Zones gives each climate region its own ambient sound. The Lightning mode takes NASA’s ISS lightning footage and turns each flash into a note, so a stormier planet sounds busier. We also added a voice narrator called Earthy, so the globe can be explored without looking at the screen.

We think it matters because it makes Earth science more accessible and more fun to explore, especially for students.
details:
What it does and how it works

The Earth Information Jukebox is a web app built around an interactive 3D globe. It has three modes. In Weather Moods, NASA’s global precipitation visualization is wrapped around the globe and split by country borders. When you click a country, the app fetches its live temperature and wind, works out its continent and region, and classifies the weather into a mood, each with its own song. Climate Zones divides the planet into latitude bands (polar, high mid-latitudes, mid-latitudes, tropics), each with an ambient soundscape generated in the browser. Lightning mode maps NASA’s ISS lightning footage onto the globe. A line sweeps from pole to pole and turns every flash it crosses into a note, so the more lightning there is, the more intense the music. A Sound Studio lets users layer their own nature recordings (rain, wind, birds, water).

Benefits and intended impact

Earth data is usually shown only visually, which leaves out people with visual impairments and can feel dry for students. We wanted to make exploring weather and climate more accessible, more engaging and more memorable. We also added a voice narrator, Earthy, so the globe can be explored without looking at the screen. We hope it helps people, especially young learners, see the planet as something they can listen to and care about.

Tools and technologies

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with globe.gl (built on Three.js) for the 3D globe and the Web Audio API for synthesized sound. The browser’s speech synthesis powers the narrator, and IndexedDB stores user-added files locally. Data comes from NASA GMAO and NASA SVS videos, Open-Meteo (live weather), Natural Earth (country borders) and IPCC climate zones. [Add any AI tools you used, to match your SI section.]

Creativity

Instead of another chart, we turned scientific data into music, so the planet becomes something you hear. Each weather condition, climate region and lightning storm has its own sound.

What we considered

Accessibility (sound, narration and keyboard use), keeping everything running in the browser without installing anything, the privacy of user files (they never leave the browser), and crediting every NASA data source clearly.
